heard: Six survived the R-101 crash, two escaped from inside the burning airship. In 1930, R-101 left England for India with Britain's Air Minister aboard. After its final refit, it flew just 17 hours of trials without a full-speed test. In rain and wind over northern France it twice dived. It struck the ground, caught fire and 48 people died. Four engineers escaped external engine cars, the other two came from inside the hull. Exactly what triggered its first dive remains disputed.
